newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Energy Corp to close small refinery.
newsitem.headline: Japan Energy Corp to close small refinery.

text.p: Refiner Japan Energy Corp said on Friday it planned to halt processing crude oil at its small 6,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) Funagawa refinery in Akita, in northern Japan, due to its lack of profitability.
"We plan to stop refining crude at the Funagawa refinery but have not decided when," a Japan Energy spokesman said.
He said the refinery, which was constructed in 1939, is dedicated to processing domestic crude.
Availabilty of domestic crude has fallen drastically and the Funagawa refinery has been processing crude only five to six days a month in recent years, he said.
Japan Energy currently buys about 60,000 kilolitres of domestic crude a year, but will cease buying Japanese oil once the Funagawa refinery stops operating, the spokesman said.
Output of lubricant oils and biotechnology products will continue at the plant, which will also maintain its function as an oil terminal, he said.
